exact_example: Set R=C[epsilon]/(epsilon^2), D=Spec(R), Y=P3_C×D, H=P3_C×{epsilon=0}, and x=(p,epsilon=0) for a C-rational point p of P3.
D is the closed double point V(S1^2) in P1_C. Thus Y is closed in P3_C×P1_C and then in P7_C by the Segre map; Y is projective over C. Its underlying space is P3_C, so dim(Y)=3.

At x the local ring is A=(C[epsilon,u,v,w]/(epsilon^2))_(epsilon,u,v,w). Its maximal ideal modulo its square has the four independent classes epsilon,u,v,w, while its Krull dimension is3. Thus x is singular and its reduced structure sheaf has stalk k=A/(epsilon,u,v,w)=C.
exact_Grothendieck_group_map: The canonical morphism Phi:K0(Perf(Y))→G0(Y) sends [P] to the alternating sum Σ_j(-1)^j[H^j(P)].
Let J=(epsilon)⊂O_Y. Multiplication by epsilon identifies O_H with J as O_Y-modules, globally. The short exact sequence0→J→O_Y→O_H→0 gives a distinguished triangle.
For every object P of Perf(Y), derived tensor with that triangle gives F→P→F, with F=P tensor^L_OY O_H; the first F is identified with P tensor^L J by multiplication by epsilon.
Euler characteristic chi:G0(Y)→Z is additive on this triangle and chi(P)=2chi(F). The image of chi∘Phi is contained in2Z.

The skyscraper O_x has H0=C and no higher cohomology, so chi(O_x)=1. Therefore [O_x] has no preimage under Phi. This proves the failure of the specified input map without claiming that no other extension of Chern classes can be defined.
exact_local_resolution: Over R, the augmented complex ...→R --epsilon→ R --epsilon→ R→C→0 is exact: the kernel and image of multiplication by epsilon are both(epsilon).
Extend this free resolution to R[u,v,w] and localize at(epsilon,u,v,w); its homology in degree0 is C[u,v,w]_(u,v,w).
Tensor its terms with the three-variable Koszul complex on u,v,w. The total complex resolves k: the first homology computation reduces it to the Koszul resolution of C over C[u,v,w]_(u,v,w).

Every differential entry lies in the maximal ideal, so tensoring with k annihilates all differentials. The rank in degree n is Σ_(j=0)^min(3,n) binomial(3,j), hence8 for n≥3. Thus Tor_n^A(k,k)=k^8 for every n≥3.

The derived-fibre functor k tensor^L_A(-) sends each bounded finite-free representative to a bounded complex. Its value on k is unbounded by the preceding calculation. Consequently O_x is outside the perfect-complex input through this explicitly specified functor.
